subject: Edge-case latency sprint — proposal & test matrix
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Bennett <olivia@pentara.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Dec 2029 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Edge-case latency sprint — proposal & test matrix

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight plan to validate the p95/p99 gap you observed vs the hyperscaler.

Summary from call:
- Pentara saw a consistent p95 delta (~40–70ms) on short chat workloads and occasional p99 microbursts tied to bursts of concurrent small requests (~50–200 tokens).
- Your infra team can run a sandbox lab window next Tue/Wed (UTC) to lock in reproducibility.
- You asked for a short A/B plan that shows where Redwood’s runtime / routing / caching make the largest impact vs HyperscaleX.

Proposed 3-step sprint (2 business days):
1) Baseline capture (Day 1 morning) — Pentara sends 1 hour of production-like traces (sampled) + a representative prompt set (50 queries). We run identical replay against HyperscaleX and Redwood hosted dev stack to capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Deliverable: baseline table + raw traces.
2) Microburst probe (Day 1 afternoon) — Focus on small requests (<= 100 tokens) at 100–400 RPS to reproduce p99 microbursts. Test: with/without KV prefix cache; with continuous batching enabled. Deliverable: latency CDF, batching stats, and notes on tail behaviors.
3) A/B quant & routing pass (Day 2) — Evaluate a quantized model variant and a routing policy that fails over to a lower-latency region. Measure throughput (tokens/sec), p95/p99, and unit cost delta. Deliverable: recommendation matrix for production rollouts.

Goals & success criteria:
- Reproduce p95 delta within ±10ms and identify the dominant cause (batching, KV cache miss, kernel scheduling).
- Demonstrate a configuration that reduces p99 by >= 25% in the microburst window without >10% cost increase.
- Provide concrete next-step runbook your infra team can own for staging.

I attached a short plan (edgecase-latency-sprint-plan.xlsx) and a template for trace sampling. If this looks good, can we lock Tue 2029-12-10 09:00–12:00 PT for the baseline + microburst probe and Wed 09:00–12:00 PT for the A/B pass?

Next steps (proposed):
- Olivia: confirm sample trace export and lab windows (reply with S3 presign or share link).
- Kyle: provide expected RPS distribution and any throttles.
- Marcus: will send a short runbook for the replay harness and a small helper script to convert traces.

Thanks — I’ll create the HubSpot deal note and invite the lab Zoom once windows are confirmed.

—
Sergio Alvarez
